twoFactor.title: Two-factor authentication
twoFactor.codeInputPlaceholder: 6-digit code from the app, or a recovery code

off.intro: Optional. When it's on, besides your password (or Google) you also enter a 6-digit code from an app on your phone. Someone who gets hold of your password still can't sign in.

status.enabled: On since {date}. {count, plural, one {# recovery code} other {# recovery codes}} left.
status.enabledLow: On since {date}. Only {count, plural, one {# recovery code} other {# recovery codes}} left — create a new set.

setup.step1Help: Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator (App Store, Google Play). The Passwords app built into iPhone works too.
setup.step2: Step 2 — Scan the QR code with that app
setup.step2Help: In the app, choose to add an account, then scan the code. On iPhone, scanning with the Camera opens the Passwords app — that's fine, carry on.
setup.manualKey: Opening this page on your phone? Enter this key in the app:
setup.step3: Step 3 — Enter the 6-digit code the app shows

codes.saveTitle: Keep these recovery codes somewhere safe
codes.saveHelp: If you lose your phone, use a code in place of the 6-digit one; each code works once. The codes are shown only once.
codes.signedOut: Two-factor authentication is on. Every device has been signed out; sign in again with your password and a 6-digit code.
codes.fileHelp: Each code works once, for when you don't have your phone to get a code.

regenerate.intro: A new set replaces all the old codes (the old ones stop working).

disable.intro: Once it's off, signing in only needs your password (or Google).
